title: Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (FAMU)
summary: Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (FAMU) is a university in Tallahassee. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with FAMU.

sections.heading: What FAMU is known for
paragraphs: Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (FAMU) is a public institution recognized for its strong emphasis on health and business programs. Approximately 21.7% of its academic offerings are dedicated to health-related fields, reflecting the university's commitment to preparing students for careers in healthcare. Business programs also constitute a significant portion, accounting for about 12.7% of the curriculum. With an undergraduate enrollment of 7,582 students, FAMU maintains a selective admission rate of 20.56%, highlighting its competitive academic environment. The university's public status supports its mission to provide accessible education while fostering professional development in key sectors.

sections.heading: How to read FAMU tuition
paragraphs: Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (FAMU) provides distinct tuition rates for in-state and out-of-state students. The tuition for in-state students is $5,785, while out-of-state students are charged $17,725. These figures represent the base tuition costs and do not include additional expenses. The total cost of attendance, which encompasses tuition, fees, housing, meals, and other related expenses, amounts to $23,970. Understanding these numbers helps prospective students and their families plan financially for attending FAMU.

paragraphs: Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (FAMU) offers financial aid options to support its students. Prospective students can explore detailed financial aid information and use the net price calculator available on FAMU's official website to estimate their individual costs. sections.heading: Diversity
paragraphs: Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (FAMU) demonstrates a diverse student body with a majority of women, who comprise approximately 65.72% of the enrollment, while men represent about 34.28%. The racial composition is predominantly Black students at 88.51%, followed by Hispanic students at 6.08%, White students at 3.32%, and Asian students at 0.20%. Additionally, FAMU serves a significant portion of students from lower-income backgrounds, with 54.31% of the student population receiving Pell Grants. This demographic profile reflects FAMU's role as a historically Black university committed to providing educational opportunities to underrepresented groups.
